nodes.label: Measured Result
nodes.rationale: Both twins run to t=1800s from 07:00. Speeds are time-integrated (distance / vehicle-seconds), not SUMO's instantaneous mean, because the volatile figure is the flattering one and does not reproduce.

nodes.label: Time-Integrated Speed
nodes.rationale: Total distance divided by total vehicle-seconds. The instantaneous mean is a single-tick sample of two independently seeded twins and swung +98% to -4% between consecutive samples while the underlying advantage sat steady.

nodes.label: Seed And Demand Validation
nodes.rationale: Re-runs the paired experiment four times varying both the SUMO driver-behaviour seed and the underlying trips, then reports the worst case across runs rather than the mean.

nodes.label: Twin Clock Drift
nodes.rationale: The twins are separate OS processes stepping at different rates, so their clocks drift ~195s (~1%). The AI twin is normally ahead, so it has had longer to accumulate the emissions it is credited with reducing -- the live panel understates the case. Left uncorrected because a hand-applied factor cannot be audited.

nodes.label: Congestion Is Not Volume
nodes.rationale: The trams feed reports how congested a section IS, not how many vehicles are on it. An empty road at 03:00 still reports 'very fluid', so the measured index floors at ~0.45 of peak while real volume is nearer 0.10. The demand curve's SHAPE is measured and its AMPLITUDE rescaled.

nodes.label: Live Barcelona Traffic Feed
nodes.rationale: 532 instrumented sections, refreshed every few minutes, CC BY 4.0, no key. Three traps: only one of ~100 dataset resources is current, timestamps are Barcelona local with no offset marker, and state 0 means detector-down rather than clear.

nodes.label: No Default Endpoint
nodes.rationale: A plausible-looking URL invented in source would be a fabricated data source that appears to work. Optional feeds stay inert until both a key and a URL are supplied.

nodes.label: Instance Slot Instability
nodes.rationale: The vehicle array is repacked every tick and a slot holds the same vehicle only 36.4% of the time. Easing yaw from the slot's previous heading rendered a rotation more than 15 degrees wrong on 55.2% of slot-ticks. Turn rate therefore travels per-vehicle on the wire.

nodes.label: Dead Reckoning
nodes.rationale: The wire carries no vehicle IDs, so vehicles cannot be matched frame-to-frame and cannot be interpolated. Each advances along its reported heading at its reported speed until the next tick corrects it.

nodes.label: Building Coverage Trade-Off
nodes.rationale: The 3D city covers 17% of the simulated footprint. Judged on the target machine rather than the download: the file is served from localhost, so the cost is parse time and GPU load for ~30k extruded polygons on an Intel N100.

nodes.label: Demand Drift Over Long Runs
nodes.rationale: Insertion slightly exceeds what the network clears, so vehicles accumulate and the advantage narrows from +38% at 0.5h to +16.5% at 4.2h. Restart before presenting.

nodes.label: Binary Wire Format
nodes.rationale: One binary frame per tick: header JSON, then float32 per vehicle, then one byte per signal approach and per edge. JSON would be ~8x larger for the vehicle array and would stall the main thread on parse.
